nist-ir-8547.name: NIST IR 8547
nist-ir-8547.title: Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards
nist-ir-8547.summary: Quantum-vulnerable digital signatures and key establishment at 112-bit security are deprecated after 2030; all quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithms are disallowed after 2035.

nist-sp-800-131a.name: NIST SP 800-131A
nist-sp-800-131a.title: Transitioning the Use of Cryptographic Algorithms and Key Lengths
nist-sp-800-131a.status: Revision 2 (2019), with the SHA-1 retirement announced in 2022
nist-sp-800-131a.summary: Security below 112 bits, TDEA after 2023 and SHA-1 for signature generation are disallowed; SHA-1 is to be retired entirely after 2030. Algorithms outside the NIST-approved set are not approved.

cnsa-2.0.name: CNSA 2.0
cnsa-2.0.title: Commercial National Security Algorithm Suite 2.0
cnsa-2.0.summary: For national security systems: AES-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512, ML-KEM-1024 and ML-DSA-87, with LMS or XMSS for software and firmware signing, used exclusively by 2030 to 2033 depending on the kind of system.

eu-pqc-roadmap.name: EU PQC Roadmap
eu-pqc-roadmap.title: Coordinated Implementation Roadmap for the Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography
eu-pqc-roadmap.summary: Begin the transition by the end of 2026, migrate high-risk use cases by the end of 2030 and as many systems as feasible by the end of 2035.
